LESSON: THE CONSTITUTION OF KENYA

Grade: Grade 8
Subject: SOCIAL STUDIES
Strand: Political Developments and Governance
Topic 5.1: The Constitution of Kenya

SECTION 1: WELCOME

• Today’s class: The Constitution of Kenya
• How we learn: Teach → Worked example → Try this
• Use point notes. Show working. Then take the quiz.
• Big question: Why do we need a constitution?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

1. apply assertiveness in upholding principles of leadership and integrity in daily interactions

SECTION 3: CLASS STUDY (TEACH → EXAMPLE → TRY)

▸ Skill 1: apply assertiveness in upholding principles of leadership and integrity in daily interactions

Teach
• Today’s focus: apply assertiveness in upholding principles of leadership and integrity in daily interactions.
• Listen/read the idea.
• Watch/study the model.
• Then do Try this.

Worked example
• Model A for “apply assertiveness in upholding principles of leadership and integrity in daily interactions” using a school example.
• Model B for “apply assertiveness in upholding principles of leadership and integrity in daily interactions” using a home/county example.

Try this
• Your turn: show "apply assertiveness in upholding principles of leadership and integrity in daily interactions" in 3 bullet points.
• Share with a partner and improve one bullet.


SECTION: QUICK EXAMPLES

• Model 1: apply assertiveness in upholding principles of leadership and integrity in daily interactions

SECTION: PRACTICE NOW

1. Practise: apply assertiveness in upholding principles of leadership and integrity in daily interactions

SECTION: WORK TO DO

1. Make a one-page revision sheet for The Constitution of Kenya.
2. Teach someone at home for 2 minutes using bullet points only.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. Why do we need a constitution?
2. Why is assertiveness important in adhering to the Constitution of Kenya?

SECTION: REMEMBER

• apply assertiveness in upholding principles of leadership and integrity in daily interactions

• Next: complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Classroom study notes (Strategy 2)
